chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man came as a pilgrim but missed the Hajj and had not performed Tawaf. He said: 'He stays with the people in a state of Ihram during the days of Tashriq, without performing Umrah in them. When they end, he performs Tawaf with the House and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then he exits Ihram, and Hajj is incumbent upon him for the following year; he enters Ihram from where he entered Ihram.'

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Exited Ihram (ended the state of consecration)
key_terms.اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.اَلصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.اَلْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.حَرَاماً: In a state of Ihram (sacred consecration)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he misses the Hajj rituals but is already in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific ruling for a pilgrim who enters the state of Ihram but misses the core pillar of standing at Arafat, a condition known as *Hajj al-Qiran* or incomplete Hajj depending on interpretation. The Imam instructs him to remain in the state of Ihram during the Days of Tashriq without performing Umrah, then complete the Hajj by performing Tawaf and Sa'i before exiting Ihram, while remaining obligated to perform Hajj again the following year from his home region. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the continuity of the ritual state to rectify the missed pillar, distinguishing it from other schools that might require Umrah in such cases.
